intro: Six jobs, start to finish. What the caller described, what we actually found, what it took to put right, and what it cost.

cases.title: A ceiling stain that was not the roof
cases.said: Brown ring on the bedroom ceiling, growing slowly. Two roofers had already been out and found nothing wrong up top.
cases.found: Thermal showed a cooler band running away from the stain toward the bathroom wall, not toward the roof. The supply line to the shower valve had a pinhole leak soaking the joist bay and tracking sideways before it showed.
cases.did: Opened a single section of ceiling directly over the valve, replaced the failed run, dried the cavity to meter, then closed and finished it.
cases.out: One opening instead of a roof replacement. Ceiling repainted the same week.
cases.alt: Thermal scan showing a cooler anomaly in a bedroom ceiling

cases.title: A basement that flooded every heavy rain
cases.said: Two inches of water across the basement floor after any real storm. A pump had been fitted by someone else and it was not keeping up.
cases.found: The ground sloped back toward the house on the rear elevation and both downspouts discharged within a metre of the wall. The existing pump was undersized and discharging into the same saturated ground it was pumping out of.
cases.did: Regraded the rear, took both downspouts to a buried line and out to the street side, cut an interior perimeter drain to a new pit, and fitted a correctly sized pump with a battery backup.
cases.out: Dry through the following winter, including the storm that put water into two neighbouring houses.
cases.alt: Basement after interior drainage was installed

cases.title: Recurring mold in three units of one stack
cases.said: Three tenants in a vertical stack reporting smell and visible growth. It had been cleaned twice already and came back both times.
cases.found: A shared bathroom vent riser was terminating in the roof void instead of outside. Warm wet air was condensing in the void and running back down the stack, wetting the top of each unit's ceiling.
cases.did: Contained and remediated all three units under negative air, then fixed the cause: terminated the riser correctly through the roof, insulated the run, and tested air quality after the rebuild.
cases.out: Clearance passed on all three. No recurrence reported since.
cases.alt: Annotated finding showing growth and efflorescence traced to a shared riser

cases.title: A front elevation that looked fine from the pavement
cases.said: Buying the house. The inspector flagged damp on an upstairs internal wall and recommended a moisture opinion before closing.
cases.found: Pointing across the front envelope had failed and the caulking around every window and door perimeter had perished. Wind driven rain was going through the joints and into the cavity, then showing up on the inside face two rooms away from the window it entered.
cases.did: Repointed the failed courses across the elevation, cut out and replaced the perimeter sealant on every opening, and re-checked the internal wall with meters after the first heavy rain.
cases.out: Findings used in the sale negotiation before the work was booked.
cases.alt: Annotated elevation showing failed brick pointing and perished window caulking

cases.title: A common room floor lifting with no visible water
cases.said: Facilities reported the common room floor buckling. No standing water anywhere and nobody could say how long it had been happening.
cases.found: A slow fitting leak had been wetting the subfloor for months. The finish floor had been trapping it, so the moisture had spread well past anything visible from the surface and the framing below had started to go.
cases.did: Lifted the affected area, extracted and dried the substrate to a documented standard, replaced the framing that could not be saved, and produced an annotated photo report the managing agent used for their insurance claim.
cases.out: Claim accepted on the documentation. Room back in use in under two weeks.
cases.alt: Common room floor documented during removal and drying

cases.title: A portfolio survey before the winter
cases.said: The owner wanted to know which of nine buildings were going to cost money in the next twelve months, before setting the budget.
cases.found: Two buildings needed work now, one had an active leak nobody had reported, five needed only drainage attention, and one was clean.
cases.did: Surveyed all nine in a fortnight with thermal and meters, then delivered one report per building plus a single ranked summary for the board.
cases.out: Work sequenced across two budget years instead of reacting to whichever building failed first.
cases.alt: Thermal survey of a commercial elevation
